topic.title: Learned Compression and Latent Quantization
topic.overview: Learned compression builds representations that are economical to transmit or store while preserving information relevant to reconstruction or prediction. The topic combines latent-variable models, quantizers, probability coding, and task-dependent distortion measures. Lower bitrate, faster decoding, and better perceptual fidelity are related but distinct objectives.
topic.whyItMatters: The representation and the coding procedure must work together. A compact latent model may still have high latency if its entropy coding is sequential, while visually acceptable loss can be inappropriate for a downstream prediction task.
topic.evolution: Early representatives use interacting filter banks and adaptive representations. Later neural systems learn hierarchical and autoregressive priors, relative-entropy codes, and vector quantizers. A recent entropy-coding-free framework targets the coding bottleneck directly. These alternatives broaden the operational tradeoffs rather than establishing that all compression should omit entropy coding.
openQuestions: Which distortion measures preserve downstream decisions as well as appearance?
Can parallel coding retain efficiency across unfamiliar source distributions?
